## Summary
- Add `vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false'` job guards to packaged `agent-*.yml` workflows and the agent-action template.
- Document the global pause flag and distinguish it from scheduled-only controls.
- Add envelope coverage that every packaged agent workflow job carries the guard.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/docs-validation.test.js`

Closes #338

## Notes

- The implementation matches the linked #338 request: a first-class `AGENT_ENABLED=false` flag that pauses Sepo-owned workflows while leaving normal CI alone.
- The strongest rubric evidence is the envelope test that enumerates packaged `agent-*.yml` workflows and requires the guard, plus docs explaining the default and exact-value behavior.
- Smallest useful follow-up: add a link from the configuration docs to GitHub’s repository variables settings/docs so users can find where to set `AGENT_ENABLED`.

## Findings

- **INFO:** No blocking rubric-specific issues found. The only minor gap is setup guidance discoverability for where to configure the repository variable.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PASS

I checked the review threads. There is one inline comment on `.github/workflows/agent-update.yml`, and it is a good question, not a blocking bug.

Yes, it is somewhat duplicated in this workflow:

- `gate` has `if: vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false'`
- `update` also has `if: vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false' && needs.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'`

For the current `agent-update.yml` DAG, the second `AGENT_ENABLED` check is mostly redundant because `update` depends on `gate`; if `gate` is skipped, `update` will not run normally. But the duplication is intentional with the broader PR invariant: every packaged `agent-*.yml` job carries its own local pause guard. That invariant is enforced in `.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts`, which checks every packaged agent workflow job for `vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false'`.

My recommendation: keep the duplicate guard. It makes the global pause rule mechanically obvious and prevents a future workflow dependency change from accidentally leaving a job unguarded. If you want to improve clarity, the smallest follow-up would be adding a short test/comment explaining that dependent jobs still repeat the guard by design.
